A PS2 game converted for PC, this really plays much better with a game pad than a keyboard. It follows the story of Kain, once the vampire ruler of Nosgoth, now believed to be dead at the hands of the leader of the church. Instead some dubious allies spirited his corpse away and he eventually woke up weak and decidedly cranky about the entire situation. The persecuted vampires want him to save them. Kain doesn't give a damn and just wants revenge and his original station back.
It's nice playing a game where you are an unapologetic villain. Humans mean nothing to you (and the game arguably penalises you for sparing them; that tiny amount of blood DOES add up). People in power are a means to an end. Snark abounds. Despite this Kain does respect loyalty and feels more like a person with a goal than a general ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Also the setting has an interesting and unique take on vampirism, it's origins, and its affects on the world around them.

Blood Omen 2 is about Kain, an arrogant nobleman-turned-vampire. Blood Omen 2 is itself a fairly straightforward action adventure game,only with a lot more blood than you'd normally find in such a game. Kain is the main character of Blood Omen 2, but he's not the hero, and "antihero" isn't the right way to describe him either. In Blood Omen 2, Kain is not heroic in the least. He's one of the only main characters in gaming who comes across as purely evil--he is not only a vampire, but also a savage killer. Interestingly, he still represents the moral center of Blood Omen 2--unlike his foes, Kain is thoroughly sincere and never minces his words, and in doing so, he remains a very intriguing protagonist. He is brought to life by the voice of Simon Templeman, who's portrayed him in all four Legacy of Kain games. Here, Templeman hams it up as good as ever, smoothly delivering Kain's lines in perfectly sinister fashion. With a couple of exceptions, the rest of the game's voice actors don't stand out as much, and the dialogue in Blood Omen 2--which is as long-winded as ever--generally isn't quite as engaging as that of the Soul Reaver games. The plot itself isn't particularly inspired either. Kain awakens hundreds of years after the events of the first Blood Omen, in a world occupied by both magic and technology. He reluctantly joins with a vampire resistance to restore rule over the world to the vampires.

This is the 9th Nancy Drew game I have played. I played most of the original ones as a child and then played some mid series to more recent ones a few years ago. It feels like a solid entry into the series. I usually perfer my ND games a little darker than this or to solve an actual crime, but the puzzles, pacing, and characters were great so I forgive it. Plus, the lighter material made it a safe choice to play in the evening after dinner. For a ND game it's pretty straight-forward making it a nice little treasure hunt. I also thought the voice acting in this one was good and liked how the characters seemed to interact and have relationships off-screen.
Danger by Design seems like a fair game to compare it to since they were released about a year apart. The two games share the same great mechanics and features that make gameplay easy, without the idk cheesiness (I guess that's the right word) I found it Danger by Design. There's also no annoying currency system or errand running in this one making it clearly the better choice.
As I recall some of the earliest games in the series could get you stuck if you did not do certain events in order. Thankfully this is not the case here. At one point I honestly thought I was stuck, but the game took pity on me I guess and I was able to continue on. I would love to elaborate more on this, but I currently don't know how to make spoiler tags or if it's possible.
TLDR: Most of my lack of enthusiasm for this game comes from my own personal preferences. It's more light hearted than other entries so it does not have the same creepiness factor of others. However, the game play itself is solid. If you're looking for a good treasure hunting adventure filled with good puzzles, you'll probably like this.

My feelings are a little mixed on this game. For the most part, it's fun with a good atmosphere and entertaining characters. But while most of the puzzles are decent, when they stumble, they stumble HARD. For instance, there's one puzzle that never indicates to you that you can't solve it fully. If I hadn't looked at a walkthrough, I would have continued bashing my head against that puzzle indefinitely. There's also another plot-critical puzzle that is almost impossible to intuit on your own. (There are also a ridiculous number of steps to it) And the ending is a frustrating series of 50/50 chance rolls where if you mess up, you have to start again from the beginning.
That said, if you don't mind playing a Nancy Drew game with walkthrough in hand, this is a fine game. There were definitely times I felt excited and satisfied by what was happening--I just couldn't fully get past all of the frustrating game design choices. And if you love HerInteractive's interpretation of The Hardy Boys, then *definitely* pick this one up!

TIP: LVL 40-50 IS A HUGE EXP GAP UNLESS YOU START SELLING WISDOM OCARINAS OR ANYTHING OF MORE VALUE FOR MORE EXP. The developers really listen to the public and add things based on opinions.
The energy system is not a simple 10/10 where you do your 10 things and then you have to wait an hour to refill. First off, it doesn't refill on its own unless you sell goods. You can increase the max amount of energy by upgrading the counter. Best way to earn energy is to sell items you are making the most with the item racks associated with that item. I have 2 lvl 15 music racks that give +200 energy per sell and all i do is surcharge my ocarinas and still get full energy. They improved the compliment heart game from when it was +4/-5 to +4/-1 now based on if you succeed/fail.
Arena mode is the latest major add-on to this game where you line up heroes against one another and hope to win to improve onto the next arena rank for better loot bags. To get skills, the heroes have to complete specific personal quests given from the inn in order to unlock the skill. Understanding your heroes' skills can help you guess what the enemy heroes might do and figure out the counter to increase chances of winning.
Being in an activy city is really helpful since they give you huge boosts based on the current lvl of buildings. You can use the regular currency to speed up things such as upgrading times, quest times, and giving exp to heroes and workers. Gems are the "premium" currency in this game but can easily be earned by selling epic+ items on trade house for gems or pre-req items great+. THIS IS NOT A PAY TO WIN GAME!!!!

Ignoring the understandable Day 1 server downtime and a couple very minor release bugs, this game is incredible.
By far its strongest selling point, the thing that sets it apart from almost every other fighting game, is the combat deck system. Virtually every aspect of your fighting style, from moves to small combos to 12-move attack chains is fully customizable. This allows for an incredible number of fighting style combinations, and unlike other fighting games, you never know what an enemy has up their sleeve just by knowing their class.
While the PvE is relatively short and not complicated, it serves as a great tutorial, and at times can actually be a bit challenging. However, where this game really shines is in PvP. When no two enemy players have the same moveset, it really makes every fight interesting, and with all the different mechanics like alternate attacks, dodges, parries, feints, etc., the combat is extremely in-depth and fun to play.

Absolver has a lot of promise to it as a fighting, however on Launch is has such a laundry list of issues and bugs. Server stability is laughable at the best of times, and non-existent the rest.  Latency in PVP is okay...Occasionally. Most of the time though, it makes PVP an unplayable expierence, and the problem is that PVP is the bulk of this game.
Yes, there is a PVE expierence to this game, but it's going to take you 3 to 6 hours at the most to complete. The "open" world is fairly small. There is very little storied content there with minimal context as to why you are doing what you are doing. This is not a single player game, or a story driven one by any mark. The unfortunate thing is, you must spend time in PVE in order to gain certain abilties to put you on even footing in PVP.
This brings us to the issues with PVE. AI seem fairly over-powered, ( the first boss will make any new player rage to the content of quiting and asking for a refund.)  often having outrageous stamina bars, Extended hit stun on their move sets, and take very little hit stun from yours, warping your perspective on what PVP will be like, and it's vastly differently from fighting AI.
There are also a huge amount of bugs i have ran into regarding combat, such as Breaker Moves not breaking Khalts Absorb move like it should according to game description. This makes Khalt AI insanely difficult for me to deal with, as they often spam this ability to negate any move you throw at them.
Absolver does have a solid combat system, When working properly, and if these issues are fixed it will be a fun PVP Brawler, but in the current state, It's more of a headache than it is a good time.

This Game is Ridiculously BEAUTIFUL!
This game is so full of life. The graphics are great, the creatures are cute and imaginative, the land is vast and there is a lot to do! Rather than in-game currency you craft and collect things to trade with vendors! It's really easy to stock up on supplies and there are many types of teleporters to take you all over the map.
There is plenty of things to collect, and there are even holiday events! I beat the story  mode in 10 hours and am currently trying to 100% the game.
I only really have 3 quarrels with the game:
-There are no mounts, but i think i read that that won't be an issue for too long. You can have pets follow you around, but they get stuck someway or another. But again there are a LOT of teleporters that will help you get around decently fast.
-With trading being the way to get items you want is really unique in a system like this! It's cool to see a game without real in-game currency (Though items you own will have some sort of Monetary Value), however I feel that after you become a craftmaster all you really do with craftable items is trade them for more crafting materials, if not make em just for the achievements (provided there are achievements for it). Though this is more of a personal opinion I feel like there should be something like rent or such to really make you want to craft expensive items outside of trading them off.
-My last quarrel is kinda a stupid one so it's more of a personal interest. In the game you have an encyclopedia and you can look at all the animals you encounter, all the constellations you discover, etc. However the book only updates once per animal. Now my point for this is that it will tell you
=The Max Size of the animal
=The Season it appears
=The Location it is found
There is this pink girl who will tell you a bunch of random "Fun Facts" about the creatures, and i personally think it'd be funny if the fun facts were updated whenever a fun fact was revealed. BUT more importantly in order to tame animals you need to feed them. And if you don't remember what the creature likes you're kinda screwed and have to guess, or look it up. I think at the very least what food the creatures like should be a discoverable trait for the book. But of course it's not TOO tedious to find out what animal likes what since you have such a huge backpack.
TL;DR
Pros:
-Beautiful World
-Cute Creatures
-Collectibles
-Niche Trading System
-Fishing, Farming, Crafting
-Mounts are soon to be updated (At least from what I read)
-Peaceful - No monsters to fight
-Holiday events! - In game calendar
Cons:
-When sending an animal back to the farm it seems to just stay in place. (Unless of course mine was a bug.  My Bambex just stood out in the field for the longest time)
-Not much replay value (Might change over time) - IMO the game takes quite a while and there is no real way to make your gameplay differen't each time, except maybe decorating your farms differently or getting different animals to your farm. But at that point you may as well just redecorate your current farm, and you have enough farms to house all the animals.
-NPCs aren't that memorable - No NPC so far has made a real impression on me. The Sprites are cute though

Into the War is absolutely broken and has been abandoned by the developer. I was instantly awarded the only achievement upon launching the game. In order to even write this review I needed to increase my playtime, so I managed to navigate the awful main menu interface and launch my own private server.
The game actually seems like it could have been fun. I feel it would appeal to those who love high-mobility twitch shooters. I doubt the developer intended for it to be played that way but it is indeed possible and would be easy to realise with some further polish. That's where the optimism ends.
As far as I can tell the Recon sniper rifle has no magnification. I don't know if there are any explosives, if there's more than the two standard weapons, or any melee attacks. There is no buffer to firing the pistol, so it will unload as fast as you can click. Upon being shot gasoline canisters will not explode.
I'm not able to enter any kind of key configuration to check what the keybindings are as the main menu settings are inaccessible. The mouse sensitivity is really weird, so is the FoV slider, no doubt this would evoke some motion sickness in a lot of players as I can't find a way to disable the extreme head bobbing.
Into the War feels like an unfinished Unity prototype. There are untextured objects, I assume they're pickups? It wouldn't be hard to believe that most of this game was built with the aid of third-party scripts and assets. There's stuff in here like "Spectating Ragdoll2(Clone)" upon death... it's obviously an unfinished game.
It's not surprising that this game was abandoned so quickly. It is surprising that it was allowed on Steam in the first place.

I decided to write a delayed review for my favorite CoD game: CoD 5.
This is my favorite game from the CoD series, perhaps tied with the old-but-gold Cod 2. Some Cod2 maps such as Carentan, Moscow and Toujane are maps I can still, after all these years, navigate blindfolded - they were that good. In CoD 4, despite the well implemented combat system the map and feeling of the game was gone.
With a return to the WWII setting, CoD 5: World at War delivers exactly what I always hoped. The gritty WWII feeling is there, the good old familiar WWII weapons are there, the nice map layouts are there, the killer finishing moves are there - its just a pretty perfect game (when compared to the newer games). Playing multiplayer is where the fun truly shines through.
For all those younger people or new CoD fans, this game is a true gem to play.

Surprisingly innovative game, which is fun when investing a bit of time!
It need some time to get used to the game. It has some mechanics from a shoot'em'up, but not shooting on the players side. Instead some "ripple graviational deformation" are created by bombs and "inversion bombs". The ripples are visualized with a dynamic grid.
Check the official webpage, as it contains some more explanation than the ingame help.
The initial "ship" is a bit weak. Nevertheless with some experience it is possible to beat at least everything up to boss number 4, even with this ship. Tipp: use both weapons quickly one after the other while rotating the ship, therefore positioning the bombs close together.
One main shump mechanic is the move or get killed one, which applies strongly here. But as there are no long range weapons (at least the first upgradeable ones are not), it is necessary to get close to moving enemies. This is what makes up a lot of the fun of the game.
The enemies (I played up to boss 4) are all  very nice, challenging, partly innovative. Graphics is ok, a bit generic, but practical, as it does not overfill with effects which are not directly linked to the game mecanics, as many other games have.
If you are not fixed to the standard move and shoot shoot'em'ups but want to try something a bit different, while still having some of the mechanics, I can highly recommed this game.

SMALL NOTE
First off, whoever said this game's just bad or doesn't play like a shooter... didn't play much, it's obvious they probably got stuck with the "place timed bomb" power and never moved forward...
REVIEW
This game feels pretty unique as a shooter, it's not actually a shooter in a strict sense, but it feels like one, let me explain:
CONCEPT
You maneuver a creature that's made of 3 parts, a head, a body and the fins, each part has a specific power or bonus that changes the way you can approach enemies, however the point of the game is to distort the "net" of the arena so that the enemies get stretched into it and eventually explode, at the end of each stage there's a unique boss.
RPG-FEATURES
There are parts that make you place timed bombs (I'm lookin at you, bad reviewers >.>) which can be used to wipe clusters after significant stretches to the net (meaning the fins do the big job, in this setup), some that make you greatly distort the net in front of your head (which results in a very precise snipe, or shot if you like that stuff...), some wings actually distort the net to form wave-like motions which, if moving fast enough (and accurately as well) can wipe whole clusters of enemies, some others suck-in enemies while running away from them (circle works too, actually better),
there are also bodies that empower health and movement.
TACTICS
Now, combine said parts to make your own playstyle (either fit the one needed for the stage) and consider this, while "swimming" you cause waves through the net... let's pick the snipe-head mentioned previously, if aimed correcly gathering enough speed, swimming towards enemies empowers the "shot", because you are moving the waves towards them.
MONSTERS
The monsters in these arenas usually come in clusters, actually it's a single sentient being that comes with meat parts (non-moving, non-attacking), shaped parts (those shoot or attack in some motion), and purple parts (which function as the creature's brain, dispose of those and it won't move any longer).
It's also worth mentioning that whenever you manipulate the net these monsters react differently, some may come closer to you from behind, some try to dodge predicting your route, things can get hairy quickly if you don't pay much attention to how you manipulate the net because it's made by squares and less squares to travel (stretched wide net) means faster movement (ie: movement=5 squares per second).
MY OPINION
It could take a while to adjust to this game as it's rather original (which I appreciated, very), but it's rather good, especially if you are bored of the usual projectile-hell shmups (either you don't appreciate that design).
TIP
On a note, the game requires some grind to gather points to buy the different parts (so spend'em WISELY), you might want to check other players' videos to see which parts they are using and what they do, because every body part does different things (and some parts are very expensive).
The game doesn't seem to have a proper tutorial (considering the "net" mechanic), and I forgot to mention that... If an enemy gets too close or shoots, it hurts you...
ABOUT THOSE COMPLAINING MONSTERS DON'T DIE
They die from a single snipe with one of the head parts... a suck-in from some fins... waves correctly placed... basically anything done CORRECTLY works, really, yea, just one shot, now go and stretch that net.

Just Dance 2017 is the FIRST (and maybe even the last) Just Dance game from Ubisoft that was officially released for PC. So...yeah. I considered buying it when summer started and THANK GOD, summer sales started at that time, so it was 50% off the original price.
The gameplay is same like in the previous Just Dance games, except you are playing with smartphone in your right hand for tracking your moves (Just Dance Controller). You copy your selected coach's moves, based on the accuracy, you get rating with score. The task is to get the highest score you possibly can. Then you get some coins for every play. You can spend them in shop for buying new stuff.
There is also Unlimited service, then World Dance Floor, Fitness mode, Video Challenge, Dance Quest, Just Dance Machine and Just Dance mode (Versus, COOP).
Songs in Just Dance 2017 are very known, some more, some less. Just try them, you will like them!
Pros:
+ An example that excercising can be fun too
+ Competitive
+ Online dancing with other players
+ Modes
+ Happy Hour (doesn't require Unlimited subscribtion service) every Saturday (I am thankful for this, the only time Unlimited subscribtion service works fine)
Cons:
- Unlimited subscribtion service works rarely (or even not at all) properly, I don't recommend buying Unlimited subscribtion at all.
- Price... 50$? Just...Dance i guess...? It's Ubisoft, after all. And no, I don't recommend buying this game at full price. Wait for sale, I say. I know that Ubisoft paid for song licences for Just Dance, but still...
Rating the game for full price: 50$: 3 / 10*
Rating the game for half the price: 25$: 5.5 / 10*

This game is a must for every vampire fan! A story-driven dark fantasy, which makes you feel right at home in its nihilistic world. Here are the positives, negatives and neutrals:
Positives:
1. Great atmosphere. Really nails the vampire/assassin feel. The world is dark and depressing, but it's perfect for you.
2. The abilities are nice and cool. All of them are useful.
3. The games is self-contained. You don't need to play the other games in order to understand this one.
4. Great characters. Well written considering it's made in 2002.
5. Interesting conspiracy-styled story. It will keep you hooked until the end.
6. A bunch of different ways to kill enemies with cool and satisfying finishers.
7. You can pause cutscenes.
8. Kain!
Negatives:
1. Combat is rather basic. Once you learn it there is nothing more.
2. Unskippable cutscenes. This will be a problem if you die a couple of times before a cutscene.
3. Technical problems with modern hardware and software. Better play it on a single core.
Neutrals:
1. The games is linear. I think this is not bad, but for some people it might be.
2. It's more action oriented than other LoK games. Again I like it, but it might be a problem for some because the puzzels are rather basic. After all this is an ACTION-adventure game.
As a side note I'll say that the length of the game differs depending on the difficulty. In the Options->Block there is "Assisted" and "Skilled". I recommed to try them both and see that there is a big difference between them. The combat will be more engaging (or mundane) if Skilled is chosen and very easy otherwise (and thus faster game progression).
And for a final note I'll say that Blood Omen 2: Legacy of Kain made me feel like an assassin/vampire unlike any other modern game. Although dark the world feels just right for you, again things that current games fail to do.

Yonder: The Cloud Catcher Cronicles is a simplistic, relaxing game with a surprising amount of depth in gameplay. You have your run of the mill story with a nameless protagonist and both are thrown into an extremely charming world. While there is no combat in this game, there is (as I said before) a surprising amount of depth in the gameplay mechanics.
This is a crafting and exploration game period. Very (and I mean very) little character development and a small, simple story actually work to the games advantage. Instead of immersing yourself in the world through lore and backstory, you're simply thrown into this world and given the basic tools to survive. Become familiar with the flora and fauna, build your homestead(s), and eventually find the path that solves the mystery of your character's past.
You can get through the game faily quickly if you are just following the main quest. But, if you let yourself wander, enjoy the view and strive to complete this journey one hundred percent; you will enjoy many hours of relaxing music, beautiful visuals, and a symbiotic crafting system.
What I mean by that is that everything you need isn't in one spot. You have to explore to be able to craft and vice versa. It's the same with flora and fauna; you can't engage with the animals unless you are carrying their favorite food. Then after that, once you obtain animals for your farm, they produce more items to craft with. It's a symbiotic. Almost too symbiotic.
If you're not used to keeping track of many items on a to do list. If you don't like revisiting places several times. If you hate grinding out a certain amount of material all the time. Yonder probably isn't for you. All that aside, there are a couple of technical gripes I have. First, the jumping mechanic is annoying to say the least. I understand it was probably designed the way it was in order to keep the player from reaching areas in ways not intended. This game is a combination of Harvest moon, Animal-crossing, and Zelda. Some people may think this game has a serious identity crisis, but it is definitely unique in its own way. I would say this game caters more to kids and casual gamers.
Your main mission in this game is to find/collect all of the spirits in Gemea, use their power to get rid of Murk (dark aura covering different parts of the towns), and uncover secrets of your past.
The graphic of this game is fantastic, especially if you are a fan of Zelda, they are very similar. This game has 4 seasons (special halloween event available during fall), and has a weather system. There is no time limit completing the quests, so you are able to enjoy the scenenary while you explore the field. You start the game with limited clothes/hair style/hair color choices, and this is done on purpose. Later on in game, you'll be able to purchase (barter) new clothes at different town shops, and you will be able to find different colors of hair shampoos and hairstyles from opening treasure chests, and purchase special items with old kingdom coins (also found from treasure chests).
The gameplay is very chill, you have the freedom to do whatever you want. You can do side quests while exploring different parts of the map, or join different guilds and crafts items, or you can continue with the main storyline quests (pretty short, takes about 5 hrs to finish). You can grow crops, trees, and tame animals at your farms. You can also befriends the locals (npcs) by gifting them food items (I just give them potatos), and they will agree to work for you, and clean your farm (mainly to clean poop left behind by your adopted animals).
The map is quite large, and there are distinctive areas of the map, like Antarctica, the desert, and lucious grassland, etc. You are able to tame unique animals at each of the regions, and you are able to adopt them at one of your farms. There are a bunch of hidden treasure chests waiting for you to find, and you can also smash barrels and wooden chests w/ a hammer to collect items. You can go fishing at the sea or at the river (there is a fishing contest near one of the town). You can cut down grass/weeds to collect tree seeds to plant trees all over the map. You can mine ores, and barter them for goods at shops.
Overall, I would recommend this game, there is no "GAME OVER", and you will never have to fight any monsters, so technically you never "die" unless you accidently falls into the river/ocean. This actually really bothers me because the main protagnoist was part of a sailing crew, but he/she doesn't know how to swim?!

It always dissapoints me when I have to write a negative review (in fact, I think I've only written two of them), but this game deserves it. Not because it's broken, no (even thought it is), but because it's been literally abandoned. If you go to the forums, you'll see a post from the dev explaining the situation, and how he received a lot of hate and such, which is why he decided to abandon it. He even took down the game only for it to reappear later, and made a post telling people not to buy it. On one hand, that seems reasonable; as he didn't try to scam anyone by selling a broken game. On the other, simply abandoning a project because some people disliked it or whatever isn't correct, in my opinion.
Now, to properly get into a review, and talk about the actual game, there's not much to say. Pretty much the whole game is broken or buggy. The main menu has overlapping buttons, and none of them work, other than the Multiplayer and Exit buttons. I guess the dev wanted to add a singleplayer campaign but never got around to it. When you get to multiplayer, it's fairly simple: pick a class, pick a side, and off to battle with you. It doesn't offer much, as there's only two maps, and a handful of gamemodes typical for most shooters: capture the flag, team deathmatch, and free for all. I tried the capture the flag one, as there weren't any active servers, and picking up the enemy flag (represented by a flag on a large flagpole) actually had you carrying the whole flagpole, which simply followed you around.
All in all, this seems like a really early concept for a game that never got off the ground.

Hello People,
I have played a lot of Gothic (1,2,3 and 4) since I was seven years old and after that long time I have to say, that this is still a good RPG.
I want to start with the Graphics.
The Graphic I thing is absolute acceptable, still today, but remember that the games is from 2006. Grass, Trees, Rocks and Stones look not bad and also the enemies are designed well , much better than in some other RPGs today!
There is one compromise you need to accept: the drawdistance is not that good and just load the things when you are close enough to them. But such things you can fix with Community Patchen, but more later.
For an game from 2006 there are a lot, lot of items you can find, buy, trade and gain from quests. Weapons for example looks very different and there is a big amount of them.
This continues with the other categories in your inventory that is split in five parts: weapons, armor, magic, potions and at least other stuff. All in one in your inventory you have a great overview of your loot.
If your claim is very high I have to disappoint you. The story is not that bad but also not that good.
There is no visible and typical main story like in other games but the quantity of the quests is really high. While hunting the questgoals you are able to walking through beautiful landscapes where you ever can find new quest.
My personal problem is, that the most quests can get boring because the system is like: accept quest -> walk to the destination -> battle some people/ monsters -> get back and gain your reward.
But in my opinion it is acceptable.
My last point is the community and I have to say I like it. Gothic had his biggest success mostly just in germany so the community has its limits.
We got a "Community Patch Team" that brought out a lot of bug fixes at first and continued with like new textures and better performance for newer PC configuration like we have today.
Also we have a "Community Story Project" that gave us some new quest with selfmade dialoges.
All in one Gothic 3 made my childhood. I had a lot of fun and I can highly recomment it. It's still a good game!

The atmosphere of Gothic 3 is amazing! Bright vibrant scenery, awesome/relaxing soundtrack, and NPCs act like real people.

The combat.....The combat is usually the focus point of many of the reviews. Some call it clunky, random, broken. But I will tell you that the combat isnt as bad as people make it seem. All in all I highly recommend you give this game a go! I think you will be just as surprised as I was about how fun it is! And REALLY try at the game. Dont just toss it aside after you die once. When it comes to videogames, the phrase "not for everyone" gets thrown around A LOT. After spending as much time as I could stand with Qualia 3, I have to ask, who is this for?
Somewhere in the deepest darkest part of the ocean, something really boring and annoying is happening. You're some sort of microscopic organism, and you have to destroy amoebas with bombs. Actually strike that, you don't destroy them with the actual explosions, you uh..smash(?) them with the ripple effect? It's like some interactive visual simulator, but it's also a game. You have a health meter, you can die, and most of the achievements involve taking no damage or finishing stages quickly.
I'm going to lay out what your experience with this game is going to be like. You'll play the first stage, you'll have this look on your face like you just saw a horrific car accident. The cause of the accident was a drunk cat. Do you ask yourself  "Why was a cat driving a car?" or "Why was it drunk?" Before long the questions pile up:
"Who gave a cat a drivers license?"
"Was the cat at a bar?"
"Which bar?"
"How are the drinks?"
"Any attractive women?"
And then you complete stage 1. No really, I think the purpose of that stage was to wander in circles while trying to ineffectively destroy amoebas with the ripple
Nothing seems to make sense but it doesn't matter, because you beat the first stage. You're on the winning road.
For completing trophies you're rewarded with cash. This is where most of your money is going to come from, so spend it wisely. One of the weapons you're given at first is the ability to absorb ripples. I guess this is supposed to improve the ripples of the bombs you place. Wouldn't it be better to simply have more explosions? So you buy the upgrade that spreads a bunch of bombs over a small area. This proves to be effective in stage 2. You're clearing those amoeba far more quickly than before.
But then you reach the stage 2 boss, and...that's it. The game is over, pack it up, throw it out the window. Why? Unless you've actually managed to figure out the mystery of the ripples, you'll spend the boss fight doing next to no damage. You'll place bombs like a nutty peanut, create a ton of ripples, but nothing will happen. I looked on youtube for some strats. Sure enough there's a guy that actually speedruns this game. He uses a weapon that creates ripple WAVES. He presses a button and the ripples smash entire lines of amoeba with ease. This thing is 10,000 times more effective than fiddling with bombs. Unfortunately it's really dang expensive. With enough grinding and a few more trophies you could probably afford that weapon, and go on to complete the game.
Or you'll just play something else, something that's actually enjoyable within seconds of pressing the start button instead of not at all. Qualia 3 is an enigma. Who does this appeal to? Is there more to it? Why is it so obtuse? You can be like me and allow the questions to form a mountain, a mountain that eventually crushes your skull. You could also be unlike me and not bother with this game in the first place.

The Qualia 3 Steam store front reads "Qualia 3 is a 2D, shoot-’em-up game that brings a few unique elements to the classic genre.".  Attention: Qualia 3 is not a shoot em up nor is there any semblance of or association with the classic shump genre.  An outright hoax to appeal to and lure shump fans.
Tedius game-play has you placing explosives with a customizable ship in a quasi wire-frame wave based arena.  Conceptually, the bomb induced wire-frame waves damage and will ultimately destroy the evil denizens which in turn drop the currency utilized by the customization system.   The ship customization options cost mucho dinero but you'll un-install Qualia before you customize anything.
The presentation is rendered in a 1024x768 window or full screen in the same non customizable resolution making windowed play optimal solely for crisper 1024x768 visuals.  For what it is worth Qualia does offer Steam integration, offering achievements and cloud based saving.
Unless you have a desire to watch a wave based wire-frame, Qualia wallows in tedium. Steam offers many far superior arena based alternatives including Mutant Storm Reloaded, Geometry Wars, Waves, Ultratron and Everyday Shooter.

First thing to notice about this game I guess, is it's not pretty to look at, irregardless of how old it is. The landscapes are terrible, even for post apocalyptica, the cars are really simple, and the UI is downright terrible. Visually it really has nothing going for it. Even the sound is somewhat irritating.
BUT, you don't play this for aesthetics... You play it because of the amazing physics rich turned based combat/racing. Once you get used to the UI, this game really starts to shine. At the start of each turn you change steering, gears, weapon targetting, etc. and once it's all set watch the next 3-4 seconds play out. This gets hectic when you're racing against a large group of players.
The real beauty lies in how each action follows through subsequent turns. Made that hard right a little too hard? the next 3-4 turns will be spent countersteering, and when it works... oh boy does it work. Pulling off successful drifts, jumps, etc gives you a real sense of accomplishment. Combined with terrain realistically affecting your cars handling and you have racing that equals any AAA racing simulators.
I've been playing this on and off for the past 4 years, so don't let the steam counter fool you. I highly recommend at least trying this out. Once you get past the unfriendly UI and get to the actual racing, you'll have a hell of a time.

This is a slight recommend as this is a very niche game that will not appeal to most people.  It is also has a very unfriendly user interface and learning curve.
The game is turn based, if you want to hop in a car, drive around however you want in real time, and blow stuff up, then go check out the Twisted Metal series or stuff like that, this isn't that.
The graphics are old and not very good but functional.  The number of vehicles and weapons are pretty limited, even though this game has been live and active for years.  The gang and vehicle management is done via the website that is opened in an external browser.  The Free 2 Play aspects are not so limiting to a free player that you can't enjoy the game without having to pay as you get access to the 3 first major towns and most of the events take place there.
So why the recommend? Gameplay.  If you are looking for a turn based Car Wars type game with real physics, this is your only option and a decent one.  I prefer turn based games that allow you to succeed via your wits not your twitch reflexes.  Again, the appeal for this game will be limited to a niche group, but if you feel that might be you, it is free to download and give it a try.

I was a kickstarter backer for this product and had been very disappointed in the state of it when we were first given access to play.
Now, with the fundamental revisions of the 0.9 update, the game feels like it has finally decided what kind of game it wants to be. Bricktron micromanagement is less of an issue, building and competing is a stronger focus, and the building system no longer makes me want to roll my face around the keyboard in frustration.
Pros: Great art, well designed maps, interesting building system, huge potential for multiplayer head to head.
Cons: The AI is still pretty awful. I currently chalk it up to the massive fundamental changes that they just posted and hope they spend some time improving the brickron stalls, the narrow stairway issues, and the ability to use sentries on cliffs to completely bind up corruptron attacks. It's definitely still beta, but if they put as much work getting to 1.0 as they did getting from 06 to 0.9, it will be a beautiful game.

First off, I'm going to come out and say it. I've been playing this game for a while already. First on my phone, then on an Android emulator because my phone just kind of sucks (the price you pay for a recent, but smaller model) and it was inconvenient to constantly be looking at my phone while I was on my computer. If you think that previous gameplay on a "mobile" device is going to lead to a biased review, then so be it. But before you judge, please take a look at the hours I've put into games on Steam (all on PC), which doesn't even include all the time I spent playing non-Steam PC games. I actually prefer PC games over consoles. Mobile games are for commuting (don't worry, I don't drive!) or other travel.
But I'm not here to argue the merits of one platform or another, or to beat the dead horse topic of porting games from one platform to another. (And really, my understanding is that Shop Heroes was on PC before it got ported to mobile.) I'm here to talk about the game I've been playing for close to three months now.
One of the things I like about this game is that it isn't pay to win. Yes, I did spend $5 in the beginning on a starter kit, but that was because I chose to (reward the devs for a game that caught my interest long enough to get to that point), not because I felt I had to. You can earn gems pretty easily in the game by special hero quests (limited), bulk orders (limited), free spins on the roulette wheel (3x a day, small chance to land on gems, but there are other prizes), regular quest rewards (usually gold, but sometimes other stuff), and selling items to other players for gems.
Another thing I like is that, in the beginning, it can be cooperative (joining/starting a city) or solo play. It wasn't until I hit level 25 or so (YMMV) that I felt the need to join a city. I highly recommend joining an active city around level 20-25. (Your best bet is to check the forums.) Once you're in an active city with lots of players... If that city has a castle, your city can particpate in raids, which will give you set rewards, which also include gems. It really does seem as if the devs are making sure you don't have to spend money if you don't want to!
So far, I can say the mid-game experience is pretty good. Yes, things are starting to take a while to craft if none of the related craft buildings are active, but it usually seems as if there's always something I can be doing - putting things up for sale, sending heroes on quests, upgrading hero gear, etc.
The Facebook/Kongregate/mobile community has been pretty good in the world chats, as well. Hopefully the rest of you Steam folks will be just as nice. ;)
To wrap up... Yes, you really should give this game a try if you're into the genre. It's free, we're nice, you'll have fun! I started playing with the assumption that I'd stop within 2-3 weeks, like I do with the majority of mobile games I try. I enjoyed it enough that I've stuck around for three months!
Also, apologies if this review is a little rambling. I'm starving and was in the middle of making dinner as I typed this.

I've been playing this game for about 2 months on Android. At first glance this looks like your typical microtransactions game but really, it's not. There are tons of ways to earn gems (the premium currency) and even with them, there isn't a  need to use them to progress. Sure, you can speed things up with them but let's face it, only a 10 year old running wild with mommy and daddy's credit card will use premium currency on speed ups. It would still cost way too much to speed everything up to the point that you get to the top even twice as fast as anyone playing for free. This game also has something more or less unique. You can actually pay gold, the regular free currency you use for everything in game to speed things up by investing in your city (more on that later). Whether or not you agree with it, paying doesn't make you progress that much faster. It's not pay to win either because there's no way a person who pays anything can inconvenience a person who never paid in any way.
This game also doesn't have flashy animated graphics telling you to buy gems or sales that you can't get off the screen (ala Game of War/Mobile Strike). At most, when they have a special package or sale, it's tucked way up into a banner at the top of the screen which on the steam version takes up less than 1% of the total screen and doesn't animate and drive you insane. They also don't have any extra popups that annoy you every time you enter the game or during gameplay other than the notification screen when you log on. The notification screen serves its purpose though showing you what has been going on within your city since you last logged off. It's half a banner that has news updates, sales, and social media stuff and on the other half, your list of notifications.
Within the game, you have cities of up to 25 players. A city serves an important purpose in the game. As you and the other players invest in the city, the buildings level up unlocking more workers, faster resource generation, different types of resources, more heroes to quest with, more quests, and more levels on the cooperative event held from Thursday to Sunday every week called City Raids. The game encourages cooperation with others but without too much risk, If you feel the need to leave your city, the money you invested in the city will follow you so you don't leave anything behind as long as you were a part of the city for 10 days or longer (less than 10 days, you will lose 10% - 1% for every day you were there so if you leave after 6 days, you lose 4% etc...). Investing in your city will give both an instant reward for yourself and a collective reward for your city. The collective rewards last for 30 minutes for each increment you invest and stacks for (I believe) up to 24 hours so all of your citymates will be able to reap the benefits of the collective rewards. Instant and collective rewards also increase as the building level increases. Instant rewards are things like resources, xp, and instant reduction of timers. Collective rewards are temporary, affect everyone in your city, and include things like boosted resource production, increased hero strength, increased worker skill, and reduced timers. Instant boosts stack so you can turn your timers from hours into minutes with enough gold!
The trade house allows you to trade items with other players. You can buy and sell stuff for both gold or gems. This is where many of the players make most of their money. You can also earn the premium currency (gems) here. Item prices are capped at 10x what they are worth to keep prices from going crazy.
You can send your heroes on quests to gain artifacts which are basically another resource to craft with. You can equip them with items you craft to make them stronger and allow them to go on harder quests later. Breakability of items depends on hero and item level. If they are too far apart, things will break quickly so you can't just pay money and buy the best stuff in the game in the beginning because you will lose it immediately (even though you wouldn't be able to see the best stuff in the game at a low level anyway, even in the trade house) also if a hero level is much higher than the equipment, it will break. Investing in the inn in your city can unlock more quests and artifacts along with its instant and collective boosts of reducing the quest timers.
There is an arena for PvP combat. This is mostly optional but can also help your city by winning crown jewels which can be used to purchase permanent boosts for your city. In PvP, if you win, you gain crown jewels, honor, which is used for matchmaking and leaderboards, and if you win enough times, you get a bag with a random item. If you lose, you lose honor, that's all. No one can harm your gameplay by beating you in the arena unless you're really hurt by not being at the top of the leaderboards. The only thing you can lose is honor and honor only dictates how many crown jewels you get if you win and what equipment bag you get if you win enough. The bag and crown jewels you win will not be at the expense of your opponent. You can use the same equipment on your heroes for the arena or use a special arena set. Some items give different skills so your items for quests may be different from the arena.
Overall there is a lot to do in this game but it does take a long time. If you're not into long progression games that will take you months to get to the mid and higher levels, don't bother. If you like a casual game that you can play at your own pace and you don't have to be on or have to listen 24/7 for notifications from, give this game a shot. The community is very nice. People are always willing to answer even the most basic questions and the developers are active and involved in conversations in the discussion forums on Steam and on their Website forum. I would definitely recommend.

It's an interesting game that is both great and awful. Let me explain why.
Here's what I enjoyed about Gothic 3:
- Freedom of going wherever you want, whenever you want. No quest markers - if they say you "Far north", you just go north and think "Am I far enough? Where's that damn white ripper?" Also, freedom of doing whatever you want - you can kill an NPC that's needed for some quest, and that will be only your fault
- Freedom of character development. There are intuitive str/dex/int paths, but you can grab any perks you want
- Soundtrack, it's just majestic
- The liberation system. You can liberate towns!
Here's what I can't categorize as good or bad:
- Graphics are okay-ish. Beautiful landscapes, but plastic faces of characters, plastic weapons and armor.
- There's nothing special about the story
- The loot system is made in such way that in the beginning you only get crappy things, but the more chests you open, the better your loot
Here's what spoils the fun:
- Bugs. A huge lot of bugs
- Voice acting is poor and emotionless
- Almost no armor diversity. Both rebel and orc armors have the same model with a little different colors
- Melee combat. It goes in two possible ways - either you stunlock the enemy and kill them, or you get stunlocked and killed. Especially dangerous against groups of enemies
In comparison with Gothic 2:
I can't really explain why, but G2 seemed way more cozy. Characters in G2 had pesonalities, there was way more depth to the whole world, even melee combat was more fun than here.
A couple of advices:
Finish Gothic 1 and 2 before you play Gothic 3. Find and install the community patches for G3 that will spare you a big deal of bugs. Use alternative balancing if you want, but I played without it. You can use a bow to kill enemies from a safe spot since they can't jump, or kite them, or pick them one by one to stunlock and kill with melee.
This game is a step back from G2, but it isn't as bad as most of the people think.

(This game was provided by ArtificalRaven.  Thanks, man!)
Yes,
is an RPG Maker game using several generic assets to tell the story of a mother's love for her daughter when her daughter is kidnapped one evening. Throughout the experience, I've noticed some good and bad moments that have been portrayed in this title.
The combat system for
is straight forward, though you may find it on the easy side.  As far as gameplay goes, my biggest complaints include the level designs (as other users have commented on) and the fact that you're permanently locked in one speed of movement...walking.  (Yes, running is disabled)   For the duration of this game (about 12 hours, 15 if you're like me and like to explore and exhaust NPC dialogue along with sidequest fulfillment), you'll basically be exploring mazes only to find several dead ends.  There's also a dungeon late-game that expects you to realize that there's a hidden passage at the literal beginning of the dungeon without giving you so much as a hint to it.
I often kept wondering if there were any points of no return and I've found two of them.  One at the very beginning as you're escaping your own castle and one later in the game as you're escaping a prison (which you won't be able to go back to)...to the latter you may want to have a spare save if you're aiming to unlock the "Complete all quests" achievement.
As far as the story goes, the plot (though predictable) does have a few nice twists and the narrative is well told.  I found some of the characters to be engaging, though others would end up fading into obscurity as they no longer felt as important, though you know they were supposed to be.
The music is stock, though it seems debatable whether the character portraits are stock or original.  Understandable as some of the characters look slightly different from the ones in the game
.  It may be possible that the portraits were slightly modified, though it becomes harder to judge with the few original artworks in the game...
, as said before, clocks in at about 12-15 hours (estimating since I live in a place where I'm called away often...making mine about 18 hours) of gameplay, about the same length as an RPG like
, where I clocked in about 15 hours.  If you're looking for an RPG to sit down with, feel free to try this game out...but it's probably not worth the $10 price tag.  It goes for $1.50 during a sale.  Also, don't be scared of the trailer like I was (with that screamer at the end of it), this isn't a dark game.  Just an RPG tale of a mother rescuing her daughter.

Despite this I find the slowness of the walk more engaging here.  Since this game has a far more serious tone.  And albeit its a simple story, I find it wholly enjoyable compared to super complicated ones.  That and even though this is my second time through I will say that the final plot reveal at the end of the final dungeon surprised me still after trying to find any way to connect the dots.
That being said one of the other things that is a bit of a complaint is that the first 80% of this game speeds on by, and the final dungeon is a major slog.  Mainly since there are so many side paths.  That and unless you grind for enemies, getting all the achievements adds and extra I'd say 4-7 HOURS onto the game.  I'm not kidding about that either, I would have made this review hours earlier if it wasn't for the Calypso 1k kills and the Om 600 kills achievements.
That brings up the other reason why I didn't make this review after my first playthrough.  I completely missed Om.  Yep there is a missable character!  What's even more odd is despite this and how good he is (if you equip him with an evil shield he has no vulnerabilities) plus I believe he's naturally immune to every status effect.  He has less than I want to say 40 boxes of text the entire game, and that'd be if you include the boxes for completing quests!  He has virtually no impact on the story!
But overall I still say this is worth playing, and I hope this gets around to more people, so as to release stuff like the Laxius Force and Elendia Ceus onto steam.

Developed and published by Aldorlea Games, Moonchild is a classic style 2D RPG from one of the most prolific developers on Steam, when it comes to this genre. Suffice to say, their experience with RPGMaker and general storytelling, always reflects in the excellent quality of the games they release.

Moonchild as expected, has a fairly large open world for you to discover and it’s filled to the brim with sidequests. Most of them are diversified enough and the main storyline is intriguing too. The characters and the dialogue is fleshed out fine and I did apreciate the constant comic relief and conversations that are well written. Far too many RPGs forget to spice things up with humor, which is quite sad since this is a genre that has come up with almost every scenario conceivable. More often than not, a good writer can make the difference between a bland game made with RPGMaker assets and one that stands out. Moonchild is definitely in the former camp. Now with all the praise aside, I did not enjoy having to explore dungeon after dungeon as this reminded me not very dearly, of days long gone when I had Zubat concerns and no Escape Rope on hand.

As for the graphical details, the dev team made a good use of pre-existing assets, as well as creating some of their own. You can’t really complain that a game which has obvious classic JRPG influences, might not have good looks on its side since you’re more likely to pick this game up for its character interaction and constant travelling from one part of the map to another.

However, I have to complain about the sound selection which quite frankly did not do the rest of the game, justice. It plays on a rather short loop and when will we finally have some voice acting in these games? I know we’re supposed to use our imagination and that it takes more effort which increases the game’s cost but with so much text to read, some voice work would have provided even more value to this story.

+ Pleasant details and story
+ Steam Trading Cards & Achievements

- Generic and repetitive sounds
- Too many dungeons and mazes

Many fans of old-school 2D RPGs will enjoy this title’s story and characters. Moonchild has a few shortcomings but all in all it does provide what it can, given the asking price. Achievements and Trading Cards are a nice and welcomed addition.

- : There is a couple dialogue boxes "storage/blueprints" that isn't showing up constantly (bug?). Makes for infuriating construction. Then if you misplaced a block, i've tried to tell bricktons to delete/deconstruct it and it is not happening.

My review? 10/10
TL;DR version of review?:
Read the introductions, Wiki and watch some videos. Then give the game a shot. ASK QUESTIONS IN CHAT! Plenty of vets that will gladly teach you the fun of this game.
Long version:
Now, I've been playing this game for a few days before the Steam release. So ignore my current played time listed.
Before giving this game a shot, you need to take note that this is no fast paced twitch based shooter like you'll usually see on Steam. Give the wiki a read and take a look at some of the introduction guides and videos.
KEEP IN MIND! There are ALOT of issues popping up with the Steam release that should be fixed in the next few days. Give it some time aswell.
Dont jump on the hate bandwagon because of the graphics. Look past that and at the gameplay, physics and fun you can have.
This game is something you'll love if you enjoy turn based combat with wonderful physics. Tabletop games and pen and paper RPG's.
Half of the negative reviews shown so far are from people who didnt bother checking the guide or asking questions in chat.
People load in, dink around in options and think "Oh, this isnt fun. I dont have anything to do." They dont bother asking questions, reading up on the game and just scoff "This game is awful" before leaving.
Is the learning curve steep? Yes.
But, there is hope. I joined up just as confused as most of you. I took a wee bit of time to read up on things and gave a race a try. I then asked a few questions and quickly got assisted by some of the vets.
If half of you would take the time to ask some questions, play a few scouts with some good people and actually get a taste of the game I'm sure you'd either enjoy it or hate it.
But thats exactly the problem. Most people will join this game and assume you can get right into the action. Get mad because they cant figure out what to do, troll around in the chat for a few then run back to TF2.
Again... Give the guides a read and dont be afraid to talk in chat and ask us questions. We can gladly help you.
All I ask is before you post a review is do more than just dink around in the client for 6 minutes silently before logging off. Speak up and let someone ingame show you how this is meant to be played. Then base your review off this.
Keep in mind aswell that Sam and the crew are busy making the transition to Steam aswell during all this and doing his best to fix all the problems popping up and give you an
enjoyable experience.

First of all this is a 2007 title and it look’s like it, not that that necessarily means that it’s completely bad. I’ve ‘played’ it for around an hour and 45 minutes. I say ‘played’ because I spent I most of my time in the menu trying to figure out how to start playing the game, the game decides not to work half the time. I was eventually able to complete a whole match which I enjoyed.
- If you aren’t a really patient person, don’t a lot of time on your hands and don’t like turn based games you should probably skip this
- You actually control your vehicles movement by using manipulating the steering wheel and with the physics your car can spin out of control, I thought that was really cool
So at first I had no problem getting into the a couple of tutorial matches, You just need to click on the big tutorial button in the middle of the menu. The tutorial tips missed certain points like the fact that you need to destroy the car on the other side of the map to end the first tutorial. Also after my three attempts at completing the tutorials I initially couldn’t get into them again even though in the menu I was told that the tutorial would be starting.
-----I thought the way you control your car is cool. It took me a while to work it out. You don’t actually just click where you want your vehicle to go. You actually need to change the position of a steering wheel and throttle by dragging them with the mouse or using the arrows keys. So it’s sort of like a simulation of real controls. The game indicates where your car will move to after you end your turn. When you end your turn a few seconds will pass and the vehicles move, a little bit… lol. You have to complete a lot of turns in order to cover substantial distances, because vehicles will only progress bit by bit. You will need to adjust your throttle and steering most turns in order to avoid hazards or losing control and to navigate the environment.
-----I thought this was really cool. Your car will spin out of control if you just lock the steering wheel and max out the throttle, and stuff like that. I think going inclines can cause your car to flip too, I didn’t put that to the test yet. You can also drift and go over jumps.
-----Vehicles will have different guns equipped depending on their model, I think you can also customize the loadout. Guns can be on the front, back or sides of vehicles. Drivers only appear to be able to fire front guns. But you are able to have passengers gunning weapons in the other locations.
-----I had to figure out how to use weapons, I didn’t see any instructions. You have to fiddle around a fair bit. You need to open the management tab found to above of the throttle and steering wheel controls. Click on the weapon then the occupant you wish to assign as the gunner. If you can’t assign a gunner to a weapon it may be because it’s a melee weapon used for ramming. If it is a projectile weapon click on the weapon in the management tab again to see the firing arc and select a target by left clicking it. Then after one turn you will have the option to set the weapon to fire one time only or every turn until you say so. The weapon will fire when it’s target is in it’s firing arc, which may require many turns of repositioning to achieve.
-----So that’s what I did for the first 20-30 minutes, the tutorials. So then I wanted to get stuck into the game, I wasn’t sure how it worked. I thought it would be like an open world but you actually just appear to join events such as death-races or arena combat. I think there is actually on foot combat events for you gang members as well as vehicular combat. The game makes reference to a number of towns but I have no idea how this all works i.e. how you go to them.
-----I was initially very confused about how to actually join one of these matches, it probably didn’t help that I was tired. Anyway what you are supposed to do is click on an upcoming event, the list is pretty much in the middle of the main menu. Sometimes nothing happened when I did this, which is one of the reasons I had so much trouble getting into a match. I think this might have been because of connection or server, sometimes I was disconnected without realizing it. There is no connection status indicator or sound played on disconnect and and it’s easy to miss server messages with all the chat going on. Clicking login seemed to fix this problem sometimes. Unfortunately doing so while you actually already have a connection will kick you and make you wait 30 seconds until you can reconnect.
-----Anyway if things are working properly, clicking on an event in the list should bring up a menu. Click register and then then scroll down and click register again. This should add you to the list of competitors. In each match that I joined everyone seemed to be given a stock car. Once the countdown timer has reached about 3 minutes you will be able to enter the event by clicking play game in the same window. You can leave this window before this but you may have trouble finding it again if there are different events with similar names. For some reason a lot of events have very long countdown timers, sometimes over an hour. You will probably want to choose one that has only a few minutes to wait.
-----I have successfully joined and completed one ‘race’. There were initially two other player controlled vehicles. The other ten vehicles or so were AI controlled. Every human player needs to repeatedly end their turn in order for the game to progress, otherwise you can be sitting there waiting forever. I think all players were first timers like me. All the vehicles literally gradually inched along as the players locked in their turns. Although it was a race surprising at like turn 28 half way through the first lap, weapons went hot. So missiles began flying everywhere, but everyone quickly ran out of ammo. After around half an hour and I think about 150 turns, I think I came 5th which should have earned me a reward. But my car just disappeared and I returned to menu before the last cars finished. I didn’t see a results screen. I later joined a combat arena match but for some reason I was disconnected.
-----You can buy and sell vehicles and items from NPCs and other players. I didn’t do anything with that, it doesn’t seem to be necessary for a new player.
-----I started with five gang members. They crew you vehicles and have different stats making each of them suited to specific roles including driving and gunning. Again I haven’t played for long enough to see how this affects the game. I just allowed gang members to automatically be assigned to positions in my vehicles.
-----There is also what look's like some form of scenario editor which I didn't really get a chance to look at properly.
So yes the game has 2007 graphics. But honestly they do the job. The textures are pretty basic, but the physics are cool. The cars bounce around on their suspension when they go over uneven terrain etc.
-----The main problem is really with the interface in the menu. There is no indication when you are disconnected from the server. There is no status indicator for events that you have requested or registered for once you have left the event registration window.
So yeah they game is old but I don’t really care about the graphics. I actually really wanted to get stuck into the gameplay because I liked it. But with server issues and stuff the game just made it hard for me to actually play it. If you can join events with friends, I would like to do that. But I’m not even sure that you can at this stage. If I can get the game to work reliably I think I would like to spend more time playing it.

Upon first sight, I thought this game would be just another lackluster fighting game. What I found in this game represents years of game-changing developments in the gaming scene in regards to graphics, combos, and unique characters that invite the player to form their own opinion as to who these masked marauders really are. The player is met with a catchy song upon starting the game, which really shows the amount of thought and hard work the developers put into every detail of this game. At first, I was distraught when trying to figure out the controls. However, after taking the time to smash my hands on every key on the keyboard to fathom these controls, I am proud to say I have ascended to a god-tier status in raw skill and talent. I can see this game entering the esports scene due to the skill required to play, and becoming a multi-billion dollar franchise in the process. To see if any computer can even begin to display the full potential of the lifelike graphics in this game, I took advantage of IBM's Sequoia supercomputer. When attempting to display the graphics at the highest settings, the computer went up in flames. This game encourages one to express themselves through their extravagent, yet simple attire. This game truly sets a mood representative of the title: Foolish. Despite this, playing the game is an experience none should forget.

I wanted to complete the game before I reviewed it, but it just seems to be fighting me at every turn. The stats and mechanics are poorly explained, battles seem to run the gamut of effortless or tedious, with nothing in-between, and the dialogue is relentlessly awful.

1. Every character seems to have some little snark to throw in to every situation, regardless of relevance. This is tiresome.
2. It takes about 6 text boxes for 1 text box of information to be conveyed. The rest is fluffy, unfunny babble.
3. The dialogue has no mind for tone - hamfisted attempts at humor are thrust in everywhere.
4. The *actions/emotes in asterisks* are the worst. They're lazy. What they're attempting to convey does not even require custom sprites, and could be conveyed with halfway competent writing and eventing.
My only reprieve from the tedious, pointless battles is the aggravating dialogue (and vice-versa). This game leaves me feeling more stressed than a leisure activity should. It is not fun, and it is not even a tenth as funny as it thinks it is.

This game is in my Top 10 Favorites of All Time list. I've beaten it countless times on PS2, and only picked it up on Steam when I saw a 70% off Legacy of Kain bundle. Unlike most people, I prefer the Blood Omen games to that of Soul Reaver. Kain's games are more action-oriented, as opposed to Raziel's puzzles. And frankly, I just like Kain better.
One of the big pros to Blood Omen 2 is that there is no need to have played the first one. The world of Nosgoth is vast, heavy in background and lore, but it's given to you in bits and pieces. Kain himself awakens two hundred years after the end of Blood Omen 1, giving a plot-related reason to your learning curve. His loss of power (both of status and vampiric ability) fuel the narrative as he seeks revenge. The characters you meet will be familiar if you've played the first game; they'll become familiar quickly if you haven't. The sequel could easily have been a stand-alone game, with the sheer amount of cinematics included.
The other big thing that I like is that 2 doesn't suffer from middle child syndrome. So many games that end up in a trilogy (or more) barely have a coherent beginning, and usually an unresolved end. I believe that the game was created before Defiance was concieved, but it's still a welcome change to have a story with a real beginning, middle and end, and still be able to continue the flow of the overarching plot.
The gameplay itself is very simple and straightforward. The puzzles are barely puzzles, and the game is extremely linear. And yet, the world itself comes alive through the tale of a man who, despite being the most powerful vampiric general Nosgoth has ever seen, was nearly slain by his enemies and must recover his power while navigating a world flooded with new technology, and magic even the jaded stand in awe of.
If you don't mind adjusting to the controls and graphics of an older game and enjoy sinking into a new world chock full of exposition and character-building, this might be for you.

If you like these types of games, it's one of the best of it's kind that I've found.  It's a casual game that doesn't force you to stare at the screen forever doing nothing.  You can speed everything up using in-game mechanics, and you do not need to use microtransactions.  You can play for several hours in one sitting or pick up your progress through playing for a few minutes at a time.
You're going to click.  You're going to click a lot.  You're going to watch a lot of timers.  It's going to be repetitive.  The timers should not take that long.  If they are taking longer than you want them to, upgrade your Workers and Workstations.  Make use of the Town Hall boosts and Inn boosts and you're good to go.  I'd recommend playing solo until around Shopkeeper Level 25 exclusively because the cost of Boost the Inn and Town Hall drasticially increases when you play with higher level players.
Shop Heroes is mostly solo-player with some passive bonuses granted for playing with other players.  There's no real forms of competition, and there's really no end goal.  I'm hopeful that all of the build up of Gold and Power leads to something.  It's extremely addictive.

I've been playing Shop Heroes since Oct 2015 on FB / Android. I certainly fall into the casual catagory of player, being at level 33 as of this review. I find the game very relaxing and I've enjoyed both running a small city and now being in a medium sized group of players. I've never felt pressured to buy gems, in fact I haven't so far, although I do plan to support the devs now I can do so via my Steam wallet. Also, the community for this game has been excellent in my experience. The world chat is mostly people asking questions and getting help, from what I've seen.
The game itself is pretty well done IMO. Yes, it is a time based style of game, but nothing like most time gated games, many of which aren't much of a game at all. There is a variety of things to do: crafting, selling items to heroes, using the player trading house to make gold and gems, hero personal quests to get abilities, weekend city raiding, PvP-type fighting, town building, store improvements, etc. Working towards new blueprints of items keeps me interested on the crafting side, and Cloudcade have added quite a bit of content in the time I've been playing, as well as having quick patches for bugs.
I like the well done art style, although it would have been nice if the heroes actually wore the armor you equip them with. I know this is pretty common with this type of game, but perhaps the devs could come up with some way to do that in the future, other than just an enhanced hero version like other mobile style games.
Overall, I've found Shop Heroes to be enjoyable and it is one of the few mobile style play type of games that I've kept playing for any length of time.

You are a male or female (can shift whenever you want) shop owner that has just started. Your mission is to earn money, clear the dungeons and making all the items. You start in a town alone with a really nagging toturial that teaches you stuff.
Towns: You can move form town to town with a coldown on a day before you can do it again. A town has a mayor that is the leader and the only thing the mayor pick is what building in town will have a discount on the price and you will need votes to become mayor. Your investments in the towns before the one you are in will follow you after one day has passed.
The buildings in town: - The buildings can be upgraded with gold or instantly with gems. They upgrade things like resources per hour, higher max level on the heroes, making the heroes alittle stronger while the building buff is on, new buildings, more people can live in your town, more dungeons unlocked, new workers, higher worker levels, faster dungeon times, more to collect in the events, lower crafting time. some more resources and lower prices on upgrading everything in your shop.
Shop: - You can upgrade the size of your store that will give you the abillity to get more in your store like work benches, resource bins and visiters at one time (npc heroes). You can upgrade the number of workers you can have working for you. You can upgrade the number of item slots you can make at once. You can also visit other people's shops but you will basicly just seen one momment in the shops life, when it was last active.
Tavren: - You can send partys of heroes into the dungeons and you can upgrade the number of partys you can send into the dungeons. You can open chests you find or buy and you can dual other players 5 man partys to earn points and a bag.
Gold: - To earn money you need to sell items. You can make them using resources, buy from the market, getting gold from the dungeons raids, complete town raids that will give you and the town the reward, give npcs in the tavren, that is on time, a wheel of fortune that has 8 hour cooldown or sell the resources on the market.
You can use it to buy items on the market, upgrade your store and upgrade the buildings in the town.
Gem: - To earn gems you need to sell items or resources on the market that people wanna give gems for, dungeon raids has a chance to bring back gems, a wheel of fortune that has a 8 hour cooldown, town raids has it as mile stone rewards, watching commercials in the tavren and npcs in the tavren. You can use the gems to upgrade stuff right away, buy different things for your character, heal the heroes after a dungeon, restocking your resources and hurry everything up.
Resources: - Get resource bins to collect resources. You use them to make items. The higher level a bin has the larger amount it can store and the larger amount you can have at maximum, you can have 3 bins of the same type. The more bins the faster you will get your resources and the larger amount of maximum of that resource you can have.
